title: Question 5
stem:
The variation with potential difference V of the charge Q on one of the plates of a capacitor is shown in Fig. 5.1.
The capacitor is connected to an 8.0 V power supply and two resistors R and S as shown in Fig. 5.2.
The resistance of R is 25 kΩ and the resistance of S is 220 kΩ.
The switch can be in either position X or position Y.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The switch is in position X so that the capacitor is fully charged.
Calculate the energy $E$ stored in the capacitor.
$$E = \text{...................................................... J}$$

markscheme_points.text: (energy stored =) area under line or ½ QV = ½ × 8.0 × 1.2 × 10-4

hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in capacitors and dielectric fields connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
parts.proper_answer: (energy stored =) area under line or ½ QV = ½ × 8.0 × 1.2 × 10-4; = 4.8 × 10-4 J
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Capacitors and dielectric fields. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
(energy stored =) area under line or ½ QV = ½ × 8.0 × 1.2 × 10-4; = 4.8 × 10-4 J
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.text: Show that the time constant of the discharge circuit is $3.3\text{ s}$.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in A Level Physics theory and principles connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The fully charged capacitor in (a) stores energy $E$.
Determine the time $t$ taken for the stored energy to decrease from $E$ to $E / 9$.
$$t = \text{...................................................... s}$$

markscheme_points.text: (so time to) Vo / 3 tRC o V = V e −

hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in capacitors and dielectric fields connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
Hint 4: Clearly show every intermediate algebraic substitution and ensure your final value has correct physical units.
parts.proper_answer: E ∝ V2; (so time to) Vo / 3 tRC o V = V e −; t o 3.3 o V = V e 3 − t3.3 1 = e 3 −; t = 3.6 s

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A second identical capacitor is connected in parallel with the first capacitor.
State and explain the change, if any, to the time constant of the discharge circuit.
hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in capacitors and dielectric fields that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
parts.proper_answer: (total) capacitance is doubled; time constant is doubled
